feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows real scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”  
- Good credibility through scale and specificity: 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, named tools/platforms, and concrete project examples.  
- Broad but coherent skill set: combines leadership, technical execution, governance, analytics, and content operations in a way that fits mission-driven organizations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to make the CV tighter and easier to scan.  
- Add more outcome language: several bullets describe responsibilities well but would be stronger with measurable results, improvements, or business/user impact.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak/irrelevant filler; punctuation and formatting are inconsistent across bullets/sections (e.g., bolded project formatting, slash usage, hyphenation such as “bill-level,” “member-facing,” “broadcast-quality”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly broad and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and the header subtitle.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Make the opening more specific by tying the work to enterprise-scale public-sector platforms and communications operations.
- Replace “Leads” with a first-person implied value statement and tighten the service list to the most differentiating strengths.
- Consider adding one concrete scale cue from recent experience (for example, large public-facing web environments or multi-publisher organizations).
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building enterprise web platforms, governance models and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Specializes in web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader,” “web modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled experiences” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The subtitle already signals leadership focus, so avoid overloading the intro with another long list.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and phrased with sharper, parallel wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure; avoid mixing “operations,” “systems,” and “experiences” too loosely.
- Prioritize the most market-relevant strengths first: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics and reporting systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery
- Refine the second half for specificity: Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations • Cross-channel campaign delivery
- Consider replacing “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Cross-channel communications leadership” or “Cross-channel campaign operations” for stronger seniority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; this section should complement them, not restate them.
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is close to language already used in the header and recent projects.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and skills. Tightening the phrasing and adding parallel structure will make it feel more polished and distinct.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item consistently: action + platform/output + purpose/outcome.
- Tighten wording and remove filler: e.g., “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” instead of “combining…”
- Use consistent style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for cleaner CV style.
- Consider emphasizing recency by labeling these as freelance/consulting projects if that is the intent.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video work closely overlap with the current freelance and NACo bullets; this block should highlight distinct deliverables, formats, or outcomes not stated elsewhere.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “modular structure,” and “distribution across website, email and social” echo existing competency language.

items.title: Coleman Davis
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical range, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your NACo entries. Tighten it around distinctive consulting impact, especially the AI search initiative, Drupal storytelling builds, and enterprise workflow improvements.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client value: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant to a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and cross-channel content operations.”
- Replace generic bullets with sharper outcomes: “Built enterprise communications workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.” Add metrics if possible.
- Combine technical execution into one concise bullet: “Designed and implemented Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, member toolkits, and front-end/CMS enhancements for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Make the AI work a standout final bullet: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX to improve findability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance,” “workflows,” and “cross-channel coordination” already appear repeatedly in NACo roles—keep only if you can show a new scale, toolset, or result.
- Avoid restating general web/email/social oversight already covered in your 2022–2024 director role.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management language already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening summary with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the biggest transformation: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, open/click rates, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten remaining bullets to action + result: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to strengthen decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video/studio language may overlap with earlier NACo roles; emphasize building institutional capability here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with the later NACo director role and the earlier digital media role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and concrete outputs rather than broad operational language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and video, coordinating advocacy and editorial content across multiple internal teams.”
- Tighten bullets and start with outcomes/action: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video contribution with impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership if accurate: “Standardized editorial planning and digital publishing workflows, improving cross-team coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullet.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the channel, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctiveness rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, higher-value wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Content operations leadership” if you want stronger differentiation from the header/Core Competencies.
- Keep this section purely strategic; avoid terms already covered elsewhere like “workflow design,” “stakeholder coordination,” or platform-specific language.
- If space allows, make one item more outcome-oriented in tone, e.g., “Scalable editorial governance” or “Audience-led content strategy.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” closely repeat the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of platforms and execution skills, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. Make it more selective and capability-led, with emphasis on recent strengths from the 2022–present roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw tools to grouped strengths: “Drupal & enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • SharePoint / Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal first and keep it dominant; it is the clearest recent platform strength from current and NACo roles.
- Replace “WordPress” with a more strategic phrase only if it’s still a target-role requirement; otherwise cut it to save space and avoid diluting the stronger enterprise CMS story.
- Use parallel phrasing and trim generic wording: “AI-enabled search experiences” → “AI-enabled search and content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- “CMS modernization” also overlaps with Core Competencies and recent experience bullets.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for recent leadership roles, but the item reads as a generic list. It would be stronger if framed around business use cases and decision-making impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit
- Recast from tool list to capability statement: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio and Power BI for digital performance analysis, KPI development and executive reporting.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive dashboards and decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Tighten “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and conversion performance analysis” if accurate; it signals broader optimization value.
- Consider ordering by strategic value, not software: “KPI design • Executive dashboards • Web analytics (GA4, Clarity) • Data visualization (Looker Studio, Power BI) • BigQuery • SEO/UX performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing here.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so this skills item should emphasize capability and outcomes rather than restating tools.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more specific, current, and tied to the studio/event capabilities you led most recently.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Video, Studio & Live Event Production”
- Replace with tighter, more distinctive bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and editing
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera systems and studio operations
- Virtual event technical direction and run-of-show support
- If accurate, strengthen with scale/tool specificity: e.g., “multi-camera livestream production,” “speaker-ready virtual event delivery,” or named platforms/tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” partially duplicate “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies.
- Avoid repeating broad “video production” language already supported by NACo experience; use more specialized phrasing here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize current platform depth or broadened only if it adds distinct value.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If formatting allows, add a light qualifier instead of a plain list: **CMS & web platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- If you want more impact, replace the weakest item with a more meaningful category already supported by experience, e.g. **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • CMS migration • Modular content architecture**
- Keep this section concise and platform-focused; save implementation detail for the adjacent technical item.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus the enterprise-level Drupal/SharePoint work highlighted elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools that support recent Drupal, workflow, and search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and consider removing jQuery unless it is still actively used in current work.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier in parentheses, e.g., “Cloudflare Workers (edge logic/prototyping)” or “GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation).”
- Keep this section strictly tools/implementation; let work experience carry the impact and examples.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills overlaps with GitHub Actions; differentiate or consolidate.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. Since the CV already emphasizes workflow architecture elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more intentionally grouped.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Consider shortening to the strongest, most relevant tools for recent roles: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to impact: “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and communications operations.”
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello overlap heavily as project-management tools; listing all four may feel padded unless each was meaningfully used recently.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it’s too bare to show level of expertise or connection to recent email leadership. Make it more specific and aligned with the scale already demonstrated in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing, CRM & Member Engagement Platforms
- Expand the line to show function, not just tools: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (email automation, segmentation, campaign journeys) • Higher Logic (member communications/community engagement) • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add proficiency signal such as: platform administration, campaign setup, audience segmentation, newsletter operations, reporting
- Keep the strongest/current platform first; if Dynamics 365 is most recent, lead with it as you do now

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic “email newsletters” language already covered in Work Experience; use this section to clarify platforms and technical capability instead
- If Higher Logic was not materially used in recent roles, consider dropping it to keep the list tighter and more current

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the NACo Director role. Use it to sharpen technical specificity, not repeat broad capability claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Analytics & Optimization Tools”
- Tighten content to: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboards”
- Replace broad terms like “SEO” and “Dashboarding” with more concrete tools or outputs; if SEO is important, specify “Google Search Console” or “technical SEO analysis.”
- If space allows, group by function for scanability: “Analytics: GA4, Clarity, BigQuery | Reporting: Looker Studio, Power BI | Optimization: A/B testing, Search Console”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one of the two.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 NACo role, so avoid repeating soft descriptors here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational contributions, promotion, and any measurable outputs without repeating later leadership achievements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and “firsts”: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Make contributions concrete: specify the website refresh scope, frequency/audience of livestreams or weekly videos, and any workflow improvements or production volume.
- Replace soft phrasing like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with outcome-focused language: “standardized publishing workflows,” “produced weekly advocacy video series,” “supported livestream delivery for major events.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, standardized publishing workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia, produced livestreams and a weekly video series, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating team-building/governance language already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. To strengthen it, make the scope of the research/projects clearer and emphasize the podcast as the standout, measurable accomplishment.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the second sentence and make ownership explicit: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add scale or results: number of episodes, audience/listens, internal stakeholders supported, or how the research informed programs/policy work.
- Consider a more concise final version: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia” language already covered in later NACo roles unless you add a distinct early-career angle (research, innovation, first podcast).
- “Oversaw planning, scripting, and production” overlaps with later multimedia leadership; keep this entry focused on launch/firsts.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims already established in recent roles. Tighten it toward tools/platform capability rather than broad production functions.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Tools & Production**
